title: geo-aware slowpath fallback attenuation + probabilistic shedding (hotpatch)
author: Lena Park
release_notes: Backported geo-aware slowpath attenuation and probabilistic request shedding to release/v1.18 to reduce cross-region blast radius during transient token-spike incidents. Improves SLO stability without hard-circuit trips.
description: Summary: Backport and hotpatch that implements a geo-aware slowpath fallback attenuation plus a probabilistic shedding layer for slow or degraded regions. This change avoids hard circuit-breaker trips for transient token or KV-cache pressure by applying a decaying slowpath multiplier and a controlled probabilistic shed that preserves a minimal control-plane and probe traffic. Motivation: We observed several incidents in the last month where overloaded regions abruptly opened global circuit-breakers, causing large-scale failovers and degraded tail latency across customer deployments. This PR implements a conservative, release-safe fallback: instead of tripping circuits, traffic to a degraded region is attenuated to a slowpath rate and a small fraction of requests are shed probabilistically based on SLO credit debt and recent probe success rates. Design/Implementation notes: - Geo-aware policy: decisions use per-region SLO debt windows (60s rolling) and probe health metrics; policy is intentionally conservative when downstream KV-cache misses are high. - Slowpath attenuation: introduces a multiplier (0.1–0.5 configurable) applied to routing tokens for affected regions; multiplier decays back to 1.0 over a soft-backoff window (configurable, default 10 minutes) if proxies report improving probe success. - Probabilistic shedding: uses a stochastic drop governed by (SLO_debt / SLO_budget) with an upper cap (default 0.25) and a lower floor (default 0.01) to guarantee some baseline traffic for health checks and maintain warm caches. - Probe prioritization: separate, high-weight probe tokens still flow to preserve health signals; they are excluded from shedding and count towards healing windows. - KV-cache protection: when cache miss rate > threshold, shed favors non-cacheable API patterns first (e.g., long-stream/payload-heavy routes). - Backport constraints: no surface API changes; all knobs are flags and environment-controlled, added feature-flag gate for release rollout. - Telemetry: new metrics (geo_slowpath_active, geo_shed_rate, geo_slo_debt, geo_probe_success) and logs added to the observability pipeline. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-5724) - [x] Unit tests for policy calculations - [x] Integration test: simulated multi-region pressure - [x] Metrics emitted and dashboard updated - [x] Feature gated and default-off for customer-configs - [x] Backported to release/v1.18 (hotpatch) Commits (high level): - feat(geo-fallback): add region SLO debt window & probe inputs - feat(attenuator): slowpath multiplier implementation and decay scheduler - feat(shedding): probabilistic shedding controller (configurable cap/floor) - test: add unit tests and integration harness scenarios - ci: add canary checks for metric emission Changed areas (summary): - services/routing/geo_policy.go (+312/-44): new decision graph and decay scheduler. - services/routing/attenuator.go (+178/-12): multiplier application and config plumbing. - services/routing/shedding_controller.go (+254/-36): shedding algorithm and metrics. - internal/observability/metrics_definitions.go (+34/-0): new metric names and tags. - tests/integration/geo_fallback_scenarios_test.go (+98/-12): synthetic pressure tests and assertions. - docs/ops/geo_fallback.md (+56/-2): operator-facing toggles and escalation playbook. Small illustrative snippet (attenuator decision): func decideMultiplier(regionState) { if regionState.sloDebt < config.lowThreshold { return 1.0 } return max(config.minMultiplier, 1.0 - decayFactor*regionState.sloDebt) } Review thread (selected messages, condensed): - Miguel Santos (reviewer) 2026-02-21: "Nice approach — prefer attenuation to hard fail; main ask is to make the decay window explicit in config and ensure unit tests cover boundary conditions. Also flag the behavior when multiple regions degrade simultaneously." - Lena Park (author) 2026-02-21: "Added decay window config and expanded unit tests to cover simultaneous-region scenarios. See second commit that adds integration harness changes." - Asha Kapoor (reviewer) 2026-02-22: "Observability looks good; please ensure new metrics are tagged with region and route for downstream dashboards. Also double-check that probe tokens are never counted towards normal SLO debt computation." - Lena Park 2026-02-22: "Fixed metric tags and adjusted SLO accounting so probe-only tokens are excluded (added comment and unit test)." - Jonah Reed (reviewer, SRE) 2026-02-23: "Requested a temporary kill-switch env var (RELEASE_HOTPATCH_GEO_SLOWPATH=off) for emergency rollback. Also asked for a canary rollout to 2 internal regions first." - Lena Park 2026-02-23: "Added kill-switch and canary rollout plan to docs. Canary tests passed in staging." CI and checks: - pipeline/unit-tests: initially failed (one flaky timing-based test), rerun and passed - pipeline/integration: passed on canary scenario - lint: pass - e2e/canary: pass (internal regions a, b) - infra/helm: no changes required Merge notes: - This was merged to release/v1.18 using squash merge after approvals from Miguel, Asha, and Jonah. - Merge method: squash-and-merge - Rationale for backport: urgent reliability improvements observed in production incidents; approach is backward-compatible and feature-gated. Operational guidance (for on-call and operators): - Default flags are OFF; enable via: RELEASE_GEO_SLOWPATH=true RELEASE_SLOWPATH_MIN_MULTIPLIER=0.1 RELEASE_SLOWPATH_MAX_SHED=0.25 - Start with a canary rollout to two lower-traffic regions and monitor geo_slo_debt and geo_shed_rate dashboards. - If unexpected global performance regressions are observed, use RELEASE_HOTPATCH_GEO_SLOWPATH=off to instantly revert behavior and open requests back to normal routing. Related work: ENG-5724 (design), ENG-5788 (incident retrospective), follow-up planned: add adaptive per-route multipliers and ML-driven shed probability tuning.
